overview: onsemi is a Scottsdale, Arizona-based semiconductor company specializing in intelligent power and sensing solutions, with silicon (Si), silicon carbide (SiC), and gallium nitride (GaN) technology platforms. The company is one of the largest suppliers of power semiconductors to the automotive and industrial end markets, with particular strength in SiC devices for electric vehicle powertrains and fast charging, and is expanding into AI data center power delivery (48V/800VDC architectures). It operates globally with significant manufacturing and R&D presence in the US (including the East Fishkill, NY 300mm fab acquired from GlobalFoundries), Asia, and Europe, and sells through both direct and distributor channels.

business_model.summary: onsemi designs and manufactures power discretes/modules, analog/mixed-signal ICs, and image/sensing devices, monetized through product sales (not subscription/recurring revenue) to automotive OEMs/Tier-1s, industrial customers, and increasingly data center/hyperscaler customers. Revenue is transactional and tied to design wins embedded in customer platforms (e.g., EV powertrains, ADAS, factory automation) that create multi-year revenue visibility once won, though shipments are cyclical and exposed to end-customer inventory swings. The company has been executing a 'Fab Right' manufacturing strategy — consolidating/divesting subscale fabs (e.g., agreements to divest Tarlac, Philippines and Mountain Top, PA facilities in 2026) while expanding internal 300mm SiC and analog capacity — to improve structural gross margin.

revenue_streams.name: Power Solutions Group (PSG)
revenue_streams.trend: cyclical/recovering, SiC and AI data center power the growth engine

revenue_streams.name: Analog and Mixed-Signal Group (AMG)
revenue_streams.trend: growing, exposure to industrial automation, AI data center, automotive analog

revenue_streams.name: Intelligent Sensing Group (ISG)
revenue_streams.trend: mixed - image sensors facing intensifying competition from Sony in CMOS image sensors, offset by factory automation/robotics/LiDAR sensing

business_model.customer_type: B2B - automotive OEMs/Tier-1 suppliers, industrial equipment makers, and a growing book of AI data center/hyperscaler customers (e.g., NVIDIA MGX ecosystem, AWS); sold both direct and via distributors (one distributor was ~10-12% of revenue in recent periods)
business_model.geographic_mix: Global manufacturing and sales footprint with material revenue exposure to China (auto/EV), broader Asia, Europe and the Americas; automotive end-market was roughly 51% of FY2025 revenue (down from 55% in FY2024) reflecting the downturn and mix shift toward industrial/AI

competitive_position.market_position: Top-5 global SiC power device supplier (roughly #2-3 among non-Chinese suppliers, behind STMicroelectronics which leads with ~29-33% share; onsemi holds roughly 20-22% share); the top five SiC suppliers (Infineon, ST, Wolfspeed, onsemi, ROHM) control over 90% of global non-Chinese SiC revenue. In legacy power discretes and image sensors it is a top-tier but not dominant player.

moat_factors.description: Ownership of SiC materials/substrate capacity (via GT Advanced Technologies acquisition) and in-house wafer fabrication gives some cost and supply-chain control versus fabless peers, though Wolfspeed and others also vertically integrate

Once qualified into an automotive powertrain or ADAS platform, products tend to stay for the vehicle program's life (often 5-7+ years), creating switching costs, though OEMs increasingly dual/triple-source SiC to manage pricing and supply risk

Fab Right initiative (exiting subscale fabs, expanding 300mm capacity at East Fishkill) aims to structurally improve gross margin versus smaller competitors, but execution is ongoing and FY2025 showed margins can compress sharply in a downturn
Decades-long reputation as a reliable automotive-grade power semiconductor supplier supports qualification into new programs

weaknesses: Not the share leader in SiC (STMicroelectronics leads, partly via its deep Tesla relationship)
Heavy cyclicality tied to automotive/industrial capex and inventory cycles, as starkly illustrated by the FY2025 revenue and margin collapse
Intensifying price competition in SiC as Chinese suppliers (e.g., SICC, local substrate makers) ramp capacity and compress ASPs globally
Image sensing (ISG) segment faces strong competition from Sony, which dominates CMOS image sensors
Elevated and recently increased debt load (TotalDebt jumped to over $5.3B by Q3 2026) raises financial leverage after years of a more conservative balance sheet
Significant exposure to China EV demand, where policy, subsidy, and competitive dynamics (BYD, local EV makers favoring domestic chip suppliers) are outside onsemi's control

growth_drivers: AI data center power delivery - management guided AI data center revenue to more than double in 2026, with new design wins across the power tree (NVIDIA MGX ecosystem, AWS, Great Wall) and transition to 48V and ultimately 800VDC architectures
SiC adoption in EV powertrains, onboard chargers and fast-charging infrastructure as global EV penetration continues (particularly in China BEVs), even though near-term SiC pricing is under pressure
Industrial automation, robotics and factory automation demand for sensing (ISG) and power products

Fab Right manufacturing realignment expected to structurally expand gross margin as the cycle recovers (divestiture of Mountain Top, PA and Tarlac, Philippines facilities targeting ~$35M of annualized savings beginning 2027, full run-rate by 2028)
Cyclical recovery in automotive and industrial end markets following a multi-year inventory correction that appears to have bottomed in late 2025/early 2026
New analog/mixed-signal content growth in automotive electrification and AI compute beyond pure power discretes

business.description: Automotive is roughly half of revenue; slower-than-expected EV adoption (especially outside China) and OEM production cuts directly hit volumes, as seen in the FY2025 downturn
Significant exposure to Chinese BEV demand and domestic competitive/political dynamics that favor local suppliers over time
Chinese and global SiC capacity additions are compressing ASPs faster than cost-downs in some periods, pressuring the segment's profitability even as volumes grow
A single distributor customer has represented ~10-12% of total revenue in recent periods; large automotive OEM customers (e.g., Tesla) are not individually disclosed but represent concentrated demand
Sony's scale advantage in CMOS image sensors pressures onsemi's ISG segment

financial.description: TotalDebt increased markedly (from the ~$3.0-3.4B range to over $5.3B by Q3 2026 per filings), raising leverage after a long period of conservative balance sheet management

Gross margin compressed from ~45% (FY2024) to ~33% (FY2025) and operating margin briefly turned negative (H1-2025, Q2-2026) due to underutilization charges and restructuring costs during the downcycle
Ongoing multi-year manufacturing realignment program carries cash severance costs (~$24M related to ~650 employees in 2026) and near-term margin drag before savings materialize

regulatory.description: Semiconductor export restrictions and tariff policy shifts could disrupt supply chains or access to the Chinese EV/industrial market
Changes to EV incentives in the US, Europe, or China directly affect the SiC/power semiconductor demand curve

macro.description: onsemi's end markets are classic capital-goods/consumer-durable cyclicals sensitive to interest rates and capex budgets
High rates slow EV purchases (financing-sensitive) and industrial capex, a factor cited by management as contributing to the 2024-2025 EV demand slowdown
Industry-wide SiC and power semiconductor capacity additions (onsemi's own and competitors') risk oversupply if demand growth disappoints again

execution.description: Multi-year manufacturing footprint consolidation (fab divestitures, East Fishkill ramp) must be executed without supply disruption to realize targeted margin benefits
Doubling AI data center revenue in 2026 depends on successful qualification and ramp with NVIDIA/hyperscaler programs that are new and unproven at scale for onsemi

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global SiC power semiconductor market is forecast to grow at a roughly 20-25% CAGR through the early 2030s (from ~$3.4B in 2026 to over $10B by 2031) on EV and renewable energy adoption, even as near-term growth has been choppy due to the 2024-2025 EV demand air pocket. Broader automotive/industrial semiconductor demand is emerging from a multi-year inventory correction into 2026, while AI data center power is a newer, fast-growing adjacent market.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - onsemi's core automotive and industrial end markets are classic cyclical capital-goods/durables markets; FY2025 showed revenue down ~15% YoY and gross margin compression of over 12 points at the trough
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high indirect sensitivity via EV affordability/financing and industrial capex budgets
key_input_costs: Semiconductor-grade raw materials and specialty gases

recent_developments.event: Q2 2026 results beat guidance: revenue of $1.604B (+9% YoY), non-GAAP gross margin 39.3%, non-GAAP EPS $0.74; management guided AI data center revenue to more than double in 2026 on new NVIDIA MGX, Great Wall, and AWS design wins

Announced definitive agreements to divest two manufacturing facilities (Tarlac, Philippines and Mountain Top, Pennsylvania) under the Fab Right strategy, targeting ~$35M annualized savings starting 2027, full benefit by 2028
Expanded collaboration with NVIDIA on the MGX ecosystem and announced work supporting NVIDIA's planned transition to 800VDC power architectures for next-generation AI data centers starting 2027
Reports highlighted continued SiC pricing competition and intensifying CMOS image sensor competition from Sony pressuring the ISG segment
Shares fell sharply (~8%) after guidance disappointed amid continued automotive and industrial demand weakness, before stabilizing later in the year

Automotive demand downturn (ex-China) and persistent customer inventory adjustments continued to weigh on results, though management signaled the business was moving past the trough by Q1 2026 with sequential demand improvement

Full-year revenue fell to $5,995.4M from $7,082.3M in FY2024 (down ~15%), gross margin compressed to 33.1% from 45.4%, and net income collapsed to $123.6M from $1,574.6M, reflecting the severity of the automotive/industrial/SiC inventory correction
Completed acquisition of full ownership of the East Fishkill, NY 300mm wafer fab from GlobalFoundries, expanding internal 300mm manufacturing capacity as part of the long-term Fab Right strategy

items.notes: Midpoint implies continued sequential growth off the Q2 2026 base of $1.604B as the cyclical recovery continues
Up from Q2 2026 actual of 39.3%, reflecting continued utilization improvement and Fab Right benefits
Driven by expanded NVIDIA MGX ecosystem design wins, plus Great Wall and AWS; positioned as a structural new growth vector beyond automotive/industrial
From divestiture of Tarlac, Philippines and Mountain Top, PA facilities under the Fab Right strategy

guidance.management_commentary: Management characterized Q2 2026 as evidence the company has moved past the cyclical trough, citing sequential demand improvement across automotive and industrial end markets through the quarter and raising both gross margin and EPS guidance for Q3. The AI data center business was elevated as a key new growth pillar, with management expressing confidence in design-win momentum with NVIDIA and hyperscalers. Commentary continued to flag SiC pricing competition and a slower-than-hoped China EV recovery as lingering headwinds even as the overall tone turned more constructive than in 2025.

bull_case: Cyclical recovery appears underway after a brutal FY2025 downturn (revenue -15%, gross margin -12pts), with Q2/Q3 2026 results beating guidance and margins re-expanding sequentially

AI data center power is a genuine new growth vector (guided to more than double in 2026) diversifying revenue away from pure automotive/industrial cyclicality, with credible design wins alongside NVIDIA's MGX ecosystem and 800VDC roadmap
Top-tier position in SiC (roughly #2-3 globally) positions onsemi to benefit from long-term structural EV and power-electronics adoption once near-term pricing pressure eases
Fab Right manufacturing realignment (fab divestitures, East Fishkill 300mm ramp) targets structurally higher gross margins as volumes recover, giving operating leverage on the upswing

Analyst sentiment has turned increasingly positive with multiple price target increases through 2026 (e.g., BofA to $138, Evercore to $137) reflecting confidence in the recovery and AI data center opportunity
bear_case: Automotive/industrial end markets remain structurally cyclical and exposed to EV demand uncertainty, particularly in China, where policy and local competition are outside onsemi's control

SiC is becoming a more competitive, lower-margin market as Chinese capacity ramps and global suppliers (Infineon targeting 30% share by 2030, STMicroelectronics already the leader) compete aggressively on price

FY2025 demonstrated how violently margins can compress in a downturn (gross margin fell from 45% to 33%, operating margin went negative in multiple quarters) — a repeat of the 2024-2025 playbook is a real risk if the AI/auto recovery stalls
Debt levels have risen materially (TotalDebt jumped to over $5.3B by Q3 2026), reducing the balance sheet flexibility that previously supported the stock through downturns

AI data center revenue, while fast-growing, remains a small fraction of total revenue and unproven at scale compared to onsemi's legacy automotive/industrial franchise; execution risk on new hyperscaler qualifications is real
Image sensing (ISG) segment faces intensifying competitive pressure from Sony, limiting growth in that diversification leg
